title: Riverboats played and Russell's memories of boat bands
summary: They list the boats Desvigne played, including the Sydney, St. Paul and Capitol, and Russell recalls hearing boat bands as a youth.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah. You ever play on the St. Paul?
On the St. Paul? On the St. Paul. I played on the St. Paul. 23.
Yeah, that's around, that's 33, 34, 35, this one here.
Now, which person, which other boats you played? You mentioned the Capitol, I believe, and the...
The Steamer Sydney was the first boat.
Yeah. You ever play on the St. Paul?
On the St. Paul. I played on the St. Paul. There was another boat. At night. Played on the Capitol. What about the JS? Played on the JS too. I played on practically all of those.
Another boat I've been wondering about, the Steamer Washington used to hit my hometown up in Missouri. Was that a St. Paul? That was St. Paul?
I never did play on the Washington, but I remember we didn't get to talk about the Washington. That was that boat too.

I've been on that a lot of times in the Capitol. I might have heard your band when I was a kid up there going to high school in 19... Probably so? 1920 to 23, if you were on that early, I don't know. Or even later, I could hear, I went to college up in 1926. Those bands would go up there. Yeah. I never paid any attention. I was studying classical music then, so I didn't pay much attention to the jazz, but I'd stand there and listen to them and be fascinated too. It's quite possible I heard your band once and don't even remember or didn't know it at the time.
